cross-013.answer: Skiff runs Tern at the Performance preset, which saves 1.8 ms against Quality (2.1 ms vs 3.9 ms); see dec-run-tern-on-skiff-at-the-performance-preset--74eqayfa83ybqpe3. The graph does not confirm the Meridian 120 Hz premise that Performance is Tern's lowest preset.

cross-015.answer: Two Efforts are no longer active. Shader compile cache and build farm is completed: dec-turn-the-shader-compile-cache-on-for-every-farm--4rr3b12b4sasdmaj (accepted 2026-03-20) turned the cache on for all nightly, on-demand and release builds, which is the Effort's stated end. Co-op rollback netcode prototype is abandoned: dec-abandon-rollback-netcode-for-co-op--46envrg0v4pdwv7b (accepted 2026-04-01) stopped the rollback prototype because re-running tide simulation on rollback frames costs 4.8 ms on Skiff, and it supersedes dec-prototype-rollback-netcode-for-co-op--2tx2s2p3sfbwj8x4.

netcode-004.answer: The team abandoned rollback netcode because rollback must re-run the tide simulation on every rolled-back frame, costing 4.8 ms on Skiff (about a fifth of the 25 ms frame), and the shrinking-window and quarter-resolution workarounds both failed. The reason depends on the world Decision `dec-run-the-tide-simulation-in-32-32-fixed-point--c5rjfcnmhne4h05e`, which keeps tides bit-identical across peers.

ports-012.answer: The ports team raised the Skiff dynamic resolution floor to 576p because caustic patterns under saltglass shimmered badly at the 540p floor, even after Tern (visible in 7 of 10 dune views versus 2 of 10 at 576p), per dec-raise-the-skiff-dynamic-resolution-floor-to-576p--fep9q7m08pp9f0bb, which was later superseded by dec-lower-the-skiff-dynamic-resolution-floor-to-504p--15esnt90gcn29enn.

ports-013.answer: Ship Tern as Lantern's only upscaler

render-031.answer: Alpha-tested foliage cost 2.1 ms in the visibility buffer versus 0.8 ms in forward+, because the alpha test runs in the raster pass with a per-pixel texture fetch, and saltglass refracts what is behind it so it needs the resolved scene first (dec-visibility-buffer-for-opaque-geometry-foliage-an--gvnvp04jgm7kbfh9).

render-032.answer: The team chose Tern because Halcyon has no Skiff build, so shipping it on two platforms would break the one-upscaler constraint, and owning Tern's code suits saltglass refraction and caustics, which need upscaler changes the team can make without vendor tickets (dec-ship-tern-as-lantern-s-only-upscaler--fmreq35nzyjc7k4e).

render-046.answer: The cost Finding that rejected virtual shadow maps (3.1 ms, fnd-virtual-shadow-maps-cost-3-1-ms-on-meridian--r6x0sdfecms7j1yg) was a capture error; with cached pages VSM costs 1.4 ms, less than the 1.6 ms of four cascades, and cascade seams through saltglass remain unsolved under CSM. Reopened on 2026-01-12 against dec-use-cascaded-shadow-maps-with-four-cascades--s5c1y9jaf275afzr; the record is dec-use-virtual-shadow-maps-for-the-sun--x8nqkn9q7eaf1ap4.

render-047.answer: Because a release-build capture put the visibility buffer at 7.4 ms on Skiff against 8.1 ms for forward+ (6.3 ms with half-rate material resolve), so keeping a forward+ fallback was no longer worth it, and maintaining two opaque paths cost about an engineer-week a month. Record: dec-visibility-buffer-on-all-platforms-skiff-resolve--k1ackk3c3275r5y1

world-036.answer: Kestrel retired the fiber scheduler for engine jobs because 41% of alpha crash reports had no usable stack (fiber worker dumps showed only scheduler frames), which blocked crash triage for beta, while a continuation-based thread pool kept workers 93% busy during tide turns, close to the 95% fibers gave. See dec-return-engine-jobs-to-a-thread-pool-with-continu--1zkc1v2x97taf50h.

world-055.answer: Kelp stays because the decision to shrink Kelp's dictionary to 1 MB for streamed assets (dec-shrink-kelp-s-dictionary-to-1-mb-for-streamed-as--yh8hktfqnyqhepew) ships it on every platform, and cold on Skiff it beats Zstandard by 1.7x. That decision also closed the reopened Zstandard option (dec-compress-streamed-assets-with-zstandard--bs1t15cygc51cpje).
